messages:
maya: Customer (AcmeApp) reports recurring mid-stream disconnects when users switch from cellular to Wi‑Fi. They see partial chunks and then the SSE stream ends with no error. Happening ~3–5x/day for some users. Attaching client-side log snippet and repro steps they gave.

support-bot: New ticket created: INC-4981 — Escalation to eng required (sla: P2).

maya: repro steps from customer: 1) Start chat generation on latest iOS app (webview). 2) Begin on carrier LTE. 3) Trigger hotspot / Wi‑Fi switch -> stream stops emitting after a few partial chunks. 4) Client shows connection closed; server logs show no explicit 4xx/5xx.

alex: can you paste the portion of the client log that shows the socket state around the switch?

maya: here's the client's console excerpt (redacted):
```
[2026-03-15T18:02:12Z] SSE: connected, id=abc123
[2026-03-15T18:02:21Z] SSE: received chunk (len=512)
[2026-03-15T18:02:24Z] NETWORK: carrier->wifi handoff detected
[2026-03-15T18:02:24Z] SSE: no activity
[2026-03-15T18:02:27Z] SSE: socket closed (code=0, reason="")
[2026-03-15T18:02:27Z] APP: reconnection attempt failed, error=ETIMEDOUT
```

raj: interesting — socket closed code 0 usually means client-level close or OS tear-down, not a server-initiated FIN. ETIMEDOUT on reconnect suggests the client retry ran into local network NAT/port exhaustion or the server rejected a resume attempt. Do we have ALB/nginx logs for that session id?

maya: I pulled the gateway logs for that timeframe: no 5xx, only the initial GET /v1/stream 200 then the connection disappears. No matching POSTs for resume because client never sends resume token.

alex: do we currently accept keepalive pings over SSE from the client? The platform sends periodic :heartbeat lines but client might rely on TCP keepalive only. If OS drops sockets during interface swap, server doesn't see a FIN, so connection just vanishes. That matches logs.

raj: agree. Two-pronged action: 1) short-term: advise customer to enable client-side heartbeat and shorter reconnect backoff so app can re-open stream quickly. Suggest using eventsource polyfill that keeps an X-Last-Event-ID or uses a small chunked ACK for resume. 2) platform side: consider detecting abrupt client silence and quickening connection cleanup metrics so we can attribute to network-change.

maya: suggested customer message (concise): "Enable an app-level heartbeat (send a no-op SSE comment every 10s) and increase client socket keepalive to 30s; on network change, force reconnect and attach last_received_token to resume." Want to run this by engineering before recommending.

alex: thumbs-up. Add one more thing: ask them to capture a packet trace (tcpdump) around the handoff if possible. Example tcpdump: `tcpdump -i any host api.redwood.ai and port 443 -w handoff.pcap` — that'll show whether client sends FIN/RST or if connection just disappears.

talia: also flag billing concern: customer worried about being charged for partial generations when stream dies mid-output. We should explain that tokens only bill for completed tokens emitted by the model; partial chunk before a hard stop may still count depending on server-side commit. Can ops confirm billing behavior for abrupt TCP close?

alex: ops / billing note: Our meter counts tokens as output when model returns them to the runtime; even if connection drops before client receives, the compute was consumed. We should document that and provide graceful client guidance to avoid wasted tokens (resume + idempotency patterns).

raj: quick repro we ran locally: emulated LTE->Wi‑Fi by toggling interface down/up on linux while streaming via curl to SSE endpoint. Observed server-side stream stays open for ~20s then connection is GC'd; no 4xx emitted. Server log snippet: `conn_id=zzz active=0s last_recv=22s state=ESTABLISHED -> GC`. That matches customer timing.

maya: customer requested code snippet they can try to mitigate on iOS webview. Proposed JS polyfill: 
```
const es = new EventSource(url);
es.onmessage = (e) => { /* append chunk */ }
es.onerror = () => { /* force immediate reconnect with exponential backoff */ }
setInterval(() => { /* send fetch to /heartbeat with lastOffset for resume */ fetch('/client-heartbeat', {method:'POST', body: JSON.stringify({lastOffset})}) }, 10000);
```

alex: looks good. Also add that they should preserve last successful token index in local storage so a resumed request can include `?resume_from=offset` header in the next generation request. We don't currently have an automatic resume API for streaming partials (we can recommend request-level resume with application-level dedupe).

talia: next steps for support: 1) Share mitigation steps with customer (heartbeat, immediate reconnect, capture pcap) 2) Offer to run a quick controlled test with their device (schedule remote session) 3) Ask billing for a one-off review if they were billed for runs during the incidents.

maya: I'll send the mitigation note now and propose a remote repro session. tagging @raj and @alex for any last pointers.

raj: one more pointer — if they can't modify client, suggest fallbacks: shorter prompt chunks (trim streaming window), or use non-streaming completion for mobile clients that are likely to flake.

alex: I'll open a perf ticket to surface a dashboard metric: "abrupt_client_disconnects_by_region" so we can correlate spikes with mobile carriers.

maya: thanks everyone. I'll update INC-4981 with the customer's decision and attach the logs. :thumbsup:
